stories.title: Local LLaMA user finds a neuron that makes Qwen-3.5-4B snarky and poetic
stories.summary: A Reddit user identified a single neuron in Qwen-3.5-4B that, when adjusted, makes the model confidently wrong and snarky but also produces unexpectedly interesting poetry.
stories.more: The post describes a specific neuron in Qwen-3.5-4B, found through manual interpretability exploration inspired by similar posts examining model internals. Adjusting this neuron makes the model more contrarian and snarky, often causing it to state incorrect things confidently. The same adjustment also led the model to produce poetry the poster found unexpectedly engaging. The author frames the discovery as an exploratory finding rather than a practically useful technique.

items.title: L11 N8147 is a neuron that will make Qwen-3.5-4B get things confidently wrong while being weirdly snarky... But also makes it write interesting poetry
items.excerpt: Inspired by some of the other brain surgery posts, I wanted to see if I could find anything interesting in Qwen. Not particularly useful to make it get things wrong all the time I guess, but I find the poetry it comes out with weirdly fascinating! I think the neuron is basically a dial for contrarian agreeable, but the contrarian snarky setting for some reason writes poems that read in an interesting way. submitted by /u/Tasty-Ad-3753 [link] [comments]

stories.title: Researchers propose LowRAM to shrink LLM KV cache by predicting values from keys
stories.summary: A new technique, LowRAM, fits a lightweight predictor at test time to estimate attention values from their keys, cutting KV cache memory without retraining and complementing existing compression methods.
stories.more: The KV cache that autoregressive decoding relies on grows linearly with context length, limiting batch size and throughput. Prior post-training compression methods have targeted redundancy across tokens, layers, or feature dimensions, or reduced numerical precision. This paper identifies a separate axis: within each attention head, value vectors can largely be predicted from their corresponding keys. It proposes value cache amortisation, fitting a lightweight predictor per head at test time to exploit that redundancy, though the excerpt does not specify how much memory this saves in practice.

stories.title: Tencent's AI chief warns AI bioweapon risk is coming, backs partial openness
stories.summary: Tencent chief AI scientist Yao Shunyu says AI will soon be able to help design bioweapons and argues for a middle ground between fully open and fully closed models, rather than closing off models entirely.
stories.more: Yao Shunyu, Tencent's chief AI scientist, warned that AI models will soon be able to assist in developing bioweapons. He argued against simply closing off models, noting that safety filters on open-source systems can be stripped through techniques like abliteration, while closed models such as Anthropic's Claude can be overly restrictive. For Tencent's upcoming open-weight model, Hy4, the company says it is instead filtering dangerous hacking-related knowledge directly out of the training data. The approach reflects an attempt to balance openness with safety rather than choosing one extreme.

stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair draws national security scrutiny
stories.summary: Nvidia is probing whether Chinese intelligence targeted CEO Jensen Huang through an affair, and reports say he hired a crisis PR firm known for handling sex scandals as early as October 2025.
stories.more: Ars Technica reports that Nvidia is investigating whether Chinese intelligence targeted Huang through the affair, raising a national security question. Wired reports that Huang began working with consultants from Heller, a PR firm known for handling sex scandals, as early as October 2025 — around the same time he was first linked to a suspected Chinese spy. Neither report available in the excerpts details the specific nature of the alleged espionage attempt or whether any sensitive information was compromised. Nvidia has not been quoted responding to the investigation in the excerpts.

stories.title: Google ships four TPU variants in a year, competing harder with Nvidia
stories.summary: Google expanded its TPU 8 family with two new variants, one keeping data encrypted during processing and another doubling compute and memory via dual-chip packaging, as it courts nearly 100 external customers.
stories.more: Google is expanding its TPU 8 family with two specialized variants: the TPU 8tx, which keeps sensitive data encrypted even during processing, and the TPU 8i Max, which doubles compute power and memory by placing two chips on a single package. The company now has nearly 100 external customers for its in-house chips, according to the report. Google is positioning these chips as an increasingly viable alternative to Nvidia's GPUs. This is the fourth TPU variant Google has shipped within a year.
